title: Build and Publish Flutter Apps Without a Mac
subtitle: A practical guide to compiling and deploying mobile applications to the App Store using cloud infrastructure.
products: free ebook: Publish an iOS App Without a Mac
html:
Developing cross-platform applications using frameworks like Flutter or React Native allows developers to write code on Windows or Linux machines. However, the final step of publishing an iOS application traditionally required owning physical Apple hardware to run Xcode and compile the binary.

Cloud-based continuous integration and deployment pipelines now make it entirely possible to build, sign, and submit iOS apps to the App Store without ever touching a Mac. This approach saves hardware costs and streamlines the release workflow for solo developers and remote teams.

Set Up a Cloud Build Provider

To compile iOS code remotely, you need a cloud-based CI/CD service that includes macOS runners. Popular options include GitHub Actions, Bitrise, and Codemagic, all of which provide native environments pre-installed with Xcode and the necessary platform tools.

You begin by connecting your remote code repository, such as GitHub or GitLab, to the chosen cloud service. Configure the build trigger to activate whenever you push code to a specific branch, ensuring your remote pipeline mirrors a standard local development workflow.

Configure Code Signing Certificates

Apple requires strict cryptographic signing for any app distributed to the App Store. Without a Mac, you must generate your distribution certificates and provisioning profiles through the Apple Developer portal and securely upload them to your cloud provider.

A common mistake is mismanaging certificate passwords or expiration dates, which halts the remote build process. Use your CI provider's secure environment variables to store sensitive files like your App Store Connect API keys and p12 certificates safely.

Automate the Build Process

Writing a clear configuration script is essential for compiling your Flutter or React Native project in a headless environment. Your workflow file should install the correct programming language runtimes, fetch project dependencies, and execute the build command for iOS.

For Flutter, this involves running commands to fetch packages and build the release archive. For React Native, you will need to handle CocoaPods dependencies for iOS by running specific script steps within the macOS runner environment.

Deploy Directly to TestFlight and App Store

Once the archive is successfully compiled and signed in the cloud, the final step is automated submission. Tools like fastlane integrate seamlessly with CI pipelines to upload your app binary directly to App Store Connect for review and testing.

Configure your pipeline to automatically distribute the build to TestFlight groups after a successful build. This provides a hands-off experience where your code goes from a local editor to tester devices through simple version control pushes.

Moving your iOS deployment pipeline to the cloud removes hardware barriers and standardizes your release process. By relying on remote runners and automated scripts, you can maintain a professional deployment cadence from any operating system.

Take the first step today by setting up a basic repository workflow on your preferred CI platform and verifying that your code builds successfully on a remote macOS runner.
